title: Capacitor charging and discharging; Graphs and data analysis; Magnetic flux and Faraday's/Lenz's laws
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS03-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; EL10-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MS03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG06-1#N.3c, MS03-1#N.15, MG06-1#N.9b, MG06-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: y-intercept
items.clue: Value on the vertical axis where x = 0.

items.label: Tangent
items.clue: Drawn on a curve when its slope at one place is needed.

items.label: Tolerance
items.clue: Spread in labelled capacitor values, often 20% either way.

items.label: Gradient
items.clue: Δy divided by Δx, taken from a large triangle; it has its own units.

questions.stem: A flat coil of 150 turns, each of area 20 cm², is placed with its plane at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of 0.40 T. What is the flux linkage of the coil?
A best-fit line has gradient 2.50. The steepest line through all the error bars has gradient 2.65 (same units). What is the percentage uncertainty in the gradient?
The south pole of a bar magnet is pulled away from one end of a coil whose ends are joined. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The near end of the coil becomes a south pole, pushing the magnet away faster.
The near end becomes a north pole, so work must be done to pull the magnet away.
No current flows, because the magnet is moving away from the coil, not towards it.
The near end becomes a north pole, and the energy for the current comes from the magnet's magnetism.

questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change. A north pole attracts the retreating south pole, so you do work, and that work becomes electrical energy.

questions.stem: A thick aluminium plate swings as a pendulum through the gap between the poles of a strong magnet, and stops after a few swings. An identical plate with many deep slots cut into it swings for much longer. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Aluminium is attracted by magnets, and the solid plate has more metal for the magnet to grip.
Currents induced in the moving solid plate oppose its motion; the slots block their paths.
The slots let air pass through the plate, so the slotted plate meets far less air resistance.
The induced currents draw energy from the magnet, which grows weaker during each swing of the solid plate.
